topics.label: IP Addressing
topics.desc: The IPv4 and IPv6 numbering scheme that uniquely identifies hosts on the internet, with subnets, CIDR notation, and public-vs-private ranges via NAT.

topics.label: Packets & Routing
topics.desc: Data split into IP packets that routers forward hop-by-hop across networks using BGP, each packet independently finding a path between source and destination.

topics.label: TCP & UDP
topics.desc: The two transport protocols beneath HTTP: TCP's reliable, ordered, connection-based byte stream with handshakes, versus UDP's fast, connectionless datagrams used by QUIC and DNS.

topics.label: Client-Server Model
topics.desc: The request-response architecture where browsers and apps (clients) ask servers for resources, contrasted with peer-to-peer, and underpinning all web communication.

topics.label: ISPs & Internet Backbone
topics.desc: The tiered network of ISPs, peering, and IXPs that physically carries traffic, plus last-mile links, undersea cables, and Autonomous Systems forming the global backbone.

topics.label: Ports & Sockets
topics.desc: Numbered endpoints (80, 443, 22) that multiplex services on one host, with a socket being the IP-plus-port pair that uniquely identifies one end of a connection.

topics.label: URL to Pixels
topics.desc: The full journey of a page load: DNS lookup, TCP and TLS handshakes, HTTP request, server response, and browser rendering, tying every web-foundations concept together.

topics.label: URL & URI Anatomy
topics.desc: The structure of a URL: scheme, host, port, path, query string, and fragment, plus the URI/URL/URN distinction, percent-encoding, and how each part drives routing.

topics.label: HTTP Request/Response
topics.desc: The stateless cycle of a client request (method, path, headers, body) and a server response (status line, headers, body) that forms the core of all web traffic.

topics.label: HTTP Methods
topics.desc: Verbs like GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE, HEAD, and OPTIONS that declare intent, with safety and idempotency semantics that REST APIs and caches rely on.

topics.label: HTTP Status Codes
topics.desc: Three-digit response codes grouped by class: 2xx success, 3xx redirects, 4xx client errors like 404, and 5xx server errors, that signal request outcomes.

topics.label: HTTP Headers
topics.desc: Key-value metadata on requests and responses controlling content type, caching, authentication, cookies, compression, and CORS, the main tuning surface of HTTP.

topics.label: HTTP/1.1, /2 & /3
topics.desc: Protocol evolution from text-based HTTP/1.1 with keep-alive, to binary multiplexed HTTP/2 with header compression, to QUIC-over-UDP HTTP/3 that avoids head-of-line blocking.

topics.label: HTTPS & TLS Handshake
topics.desc: How TLS encrypts HTTP via a handshake exchanging certificates and keys, providing confidentiality, integrity, and server authentication, with TLS 1.3 cutting round trips.

topics.label: HTTP Caching
topics.desc: Browser and proxy caching governed by Cache-Control, ETag, Last-Modified, and conditional requests that avoid redundant transfers and speed up repeat visits.

topics.label: DNS Resolution
topics.desc: The hierarchical hostname-to-IP lookup walking from the resolver to root, TLD, and authoritative name servers, with recursion and caching gating every navigation.

topics.label: DNS Record Types
topics.desc: The records in a zone: A and AAAA for IPs, CNAME for aliases, MX for mail, TXT for verification, NS for delegation, and SOA for zone metadata.

topics.label: DNS TTL & Propagation
topics.desc: Time-to-live values on records that control how long resolvers cache answers, explaining propagation delay when you change records and how to plan low-downtime cutovers.

topics.label: Domain Registration
topics.desc: Buying and managing a domain through registrars under ICANN, including TLD choice, WHOIS, nameserver delegation, renewals, and transfer locks.

topics.label: Hosting Models
topics.desc: The spectrum of where apps run: shared hosting, VPS, dedicated servers, IaaS cloud VMs, managed PaaS, and serverless, trading control against operational burden.

topics.label: Static Site Hosting
topics.desc: Serving prebuilt HTML, CSS, and JS from object storage or edge networks like Netlify, GitHub Pages, or Cloudflare Pages, with no server runtime to manage.

topics.label: CDNs
topics.desc: Content delivery networks like Cloudflare and Fastly that cache and serve assets from edge points of presence near users, cutting latency and absorbing traffic spikes.

topics.label: Reverse Proxy
topics.desc: A server like Nginx or a load balancer sitting in front of app servers to terminate TLS, route requests, balance load, and cache, hiding backend topology from clients.

topics.label: Browser Architecture
topics.desc: How a browser is built: the rendering engine, JavaScript engine, networking, and a multi-process model isolating tabs and renderers from the browser and GPU processes.

topics.label: DOM Construction
topics.desc: Parsing HTML bytes into tokens and then a Document Object Model tree of nodes that scripts query and mutate and that styling and layout operate on.

topics.label: CSSOM
topics.desc: Parsing stylesheets into the CSS Object Model, a tree of computed style rules combined with the DOM to decide how each element should look.

topics.label: Render Tree
topics.desc: The visual-only tree the browser builds by merging the DOM with the CSSOM, excluding non-rendered nodes like head and elements set to display:none.

topics.label: Layout & Paint
topics.desc: Computing each box's geometry (layout/reflow), filling pixels (paint), and combining layers (compositing), the steps whose cost reflows and repaints drive.

topics.label: Critical Rendering Path
topics.desc: The sequence from bytes to first pixels, where render-blocking CSS and parser-blocking scripts gate display, optimized with async, defer, and prioritized resources.

topics.label: JS Engine & Loop
topics.desc: How engines like V8 parse and JIT-compile JavaScript and run it on a single-threaded event loop with task and microtask queues that schedule non-blocking work.

topics.label: Browser Storage
topics.desc: Client-side persistence beyond cookies: localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, the Cache API, and Service Workers that enable offline and faster repeat loads.

topics.label: Same-Origin Policy
topics.desc: The browser's core isolation boundary keyed on scheme, host, and port that blocks one origin's scripts from reading another origin's responses and DOM.

topics.label: CORS
topics.desc: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing headers like Access-Control-Allow-Origin plus preflight OPTIONS requests that let servers safely opt in to cross-origin browser access.

topics.label: Cookies
topics.desc: Server-set state tokens carried on requests, scoped by domain and path with Expires, and hardened by HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite flags against theft and CSRF.

topics.label: Transport Security
topics.desc: Enforcing encryption end to end with HTTPS, HSTS to force secure connections, certificate trust chains, and mixed-content blocking that protect data in transit.

topics.label: Content Security Policy
topics.desc: A response header that whitelists allowed script, style, and resource sources to mitigate XSS and data injection, with nonces and reporting for violations.

topics.label: Common Web Attacks
topics.desc: An overview of the threats every web dev must recognize: XSS, CSRF, clickjacking, and injection, plus the browser defenses that blunt them (deep coverage lives elsewhere).

topics.label: Security Headers
topics.desc: Hardening response headers beyond CSP: X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy that tighten browser behavior by default.

topics.label: MIME & Content Types
topics.desc: Media type labels like text/html, application/json, and image/png in the Content-Type header that tell clients how to interpret a payload's bytes.

topics.label: JSON
topics.desc: The lightweight, language-agnostic key-value and array text format that dominates web APIs, easily parsed in every language and native to JavaScript.

topics.label: XML
topics.desc: The verbose, schema-capable markup format behind SOAP, RSS, SVG, and many legacy and enterprise systems, with namespaces, attributes, and XSD validation.

topics.label: Form Encoding & Multipart
topics.desc: How HTML forms serialize submissions: application/x-www-form-urlencoded for fields and multipart/form-data for file uploads, the classic POST body formats.

topics.label: Character Encoding
topics.desc: How text maps to bytes via UTF-8 and Unicode code points, why mojibake happens with mismatched charsets, and the charset declaration in headers and meta tags.

topics.label: HTTP Compression
topics.desc: Shrinking response bodies on the wire with gzip and brotli, negotiated via Accept-Encoding and Content-Encoding, to cut bandwidth and speed transfers.

topics.label: WebSockets
topics.desc: A full-duplex persistent connection upgraded from HTTP that enables low-latency bidirectional messaging for chat, live updates, and collaboration (depth covered elsewhere).

topics.label: Server-Sent Events
topics.desc: A one-way text/event-stream over HTTP that pushes updates from server to browser with auto-reconnect, a simpler alternative to WebSockets for live feeds.
